title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 37 (Action by Affected Persons)

content.overview: Section 37 provides a standing route: a person, group of persons or any association of persons affected by any misleading statement or the inclusion or omission of any matter in the prospectus may take action under section 34, 35 or 36 as applicable.
content.glance: Affected persons (individual, group or association) may sue under ss. 34, 35 or 36; s. 37 is a standing provision, not a separate liability head.
content.study: Section 37 does not create a new species of liability. It enables a person, a group of persons or any association of persons affected by any misleading statement or the inclusion or omission of any matter in the prospectus to take action under section 34 (criminal), section 35 (civil compensation) or section 36 (fraudulent inducement), as the case may be. Current-law framing: identify the affected claimant class; identify the prospectus defect; choose the correct substantive section (34/35/36); then apply that section’s ingredients and remedies.

sections.heading: Standing
sections.body: A person, group of persons or association of persons affected by a misleading prospectus statement or inclusion/omission may take action.

sections.heading: Substantive Routes
sections.body: The action is under section 34, 35 or 36, not under s. 37 as an independent cause of action.

sections.heading: Application
sections.body: Prove affected status; map facts to the chosen substantive section; seek that section’s remedy.

examples.title: Investor group civil claim
examples.body: A group of subscribers affected by a misleading prospectus statement brings a s. 35 compensation claim. Section 37 confirms their standing as affected persons.

examples.title: Association action
examples.body: An association of affected investors invokes s. 37 to pursue remedies under ss. 34–36 on the basis of prospectus defects.

hypotheticals.question: Does s. 37 itself create liability for misleading statements?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. It is a standing/action provision; liability and remedies come from ss. 34, 35 or 36.

distinctions.title: Action by affected persons (s. 37) vs civil liability (s. 35)
distinctions.right: Compensation cause of action and defendants

misconceptions.trap: Section 37 is a freestanding liability provision.
misconceptions.correction: It only enables affected persons to take action under ss. 34, 35 or 36.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 37 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify affected person/group/association. II. Identify prospectus defect. III. Choose s. 34, 35 or 36. IV. Apply that section. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Affected status; prospectus defect; chosen substantive section; remedy sought.

examTips: Treat s. 37 as standing, not liability.
Always pair it with s. 34, 35 or 36.
